title: Sunny and the First Star | Bedtime Story
description: Patient little Sunny the quokka sits very still as night falls over the Australian bush, watching for the very first star to appear — and when it does, she makes the sweetest wish. A quiet, starlit story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The sky above the bush was changing. The deep blue of the afternoon was slowly, slowly turning darker — like someone was pulling a soft dark blanket across the world.

Sunny the quokka sat very still on a smooth round rock in a clearing, her little paws folded in her lap. She was watching. Waiting. Because she knew that somewhere up in all that darkening blue, a star was about to appear — the very first one.

She didn't fidget. She didn't rush. She just looked, and breathed, and waited.

The gum trees around the clearing stood very quietly too, their leaves just barely rustling. A small night breeze moved through the bush, soft and cool and sweet-smelling.

And then — there.

A tiny point of light. Right up near the top of the sky. Blinking once, very gently, as if to say hello.

Sunny's eyes went wide. She held her breath for just a moment. Then she made her wish — not out loud, just a small, warm thought, sent up to the star. She wished for a good sleep. For soft dreams. For tomorrow to be just as gentle as tonight.

And when she looked again, another star had appeared. And then another. One by one they came, like little friends arriving quietly, until the sky was full of them, scattered like silver seeds across the deep, dark blue.

Sunny lay back on her smooth rock and looked up at all of them. She didn't count them. She just watched them glow.

Her eyes grew slower. Her breathing grew softer. And she drifted off to sleep right there under her blanket of stars.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, first star. Goodnight, little one.
